newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end mixed after Fed keeps rates steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end mixed after Fed keeps rates steady.

text.p: Wall Street stocks ended mixed on Tuesday after a choppy session that saw the Dow industrials whipsaw higher and then lower on news of the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 21 points to close unofficially at 5874. The Nasdaq Composite rose four points to 1215 and the S&P 500 index fell fractionally to 685.
News of the Fed's decision initially triggered a Wall Street celebration and within minutes of the announcement the Dow industrials jumped more than 30 points.
However, a wave of selling quashed the rally almost instantly and sent the Dow sliding more than 40 points before it reversed course yet again just moments before the close.
Analysts cited a number of reasons for the choppy finish.

"The rally in stocks and bonds pulled back partly due to the dollar," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers, noting that the dollar fell sharply after news of the Fed's decision.
Also, analysts noted, many on Wall Street still expect a rate increase in November and viewed the Fed's inaction on Tuesday as simply postponing the inevitable.

"The big bad wolf was chased behind the cottage but I expect he'll be back again," said Robert Stovall, president of Stovall/21st Advisers. "I'm afraid this fascination with Fed-watching will continue."
Much of the afternoon see-saw activity in the Dow was driven by a series of massive program trades.

According to Birinyi Associates Inc, which tracks program trading activity, a buy program initiated just after news of the Fed vote added about 30 points to the Dow. That program was followed almost immediately by a sell program that wiped out those gains.
In all, the firm said, program activity dragged the Dow industrials down by 36 points on the session.
Well before the market was forced to digest the mildly surprising interest rate news, it had already faced down a stunning profit warning from AT&T Corp.
AT&T shares slumped 5-5/8 to 51-1/2 after it said competition in its key long-distance telephone market would likely result in profit shortfalls for the second half.
"We had a negative suprise from one of the bellwether stocks of all time," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

Following the warning, PaineWebber, Prudential Securities and Merrill Lynch all downgraded AT&T, the most widely held issue in North America. The decline in AT&T shares accounted for nearly all the Dow's losses for the session.
Among individual stocks, leading semiconductor maker Texas Instruments surged 5-5/8 to 57-3/8. Montgomery Securities upgraded the stock to buy from hold.
Also helping Texas Instruments was news that spot prices for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips have firmed recently. Fellow DRAM maker Micron Technologies Inc gained 3-1/2 to 31-1/2.
Several IPOs drew strong buying. Cross-Continent Auto, which owns and operates six franchised automobile dealerships, climbed six points to 20 in its debut.
Hot Topic Inc, an apparel maker, skyrocketed 8-1/8 to 26-1/8 on its first day of trading.
However, apparel designer Mossimo extended its losses, off 3-1/2 to 30-1/2. The shares tumbled 6-7/8 Monday after Mossimo warned third-quarter earnings would fall far short of Street expectations.

GMIS Inc soared 6-3/16 to 23-5/16 after definitively agreeing to be acquired by HBO & Co in a stock deal. HBO provides patient care and financial and management software solutions to healthcare organizations and GMIS provides clinical information systems for managed care.
Shares in HBO & Co fell 1-1/4 to 62-1/2.
-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730
